articles.title: PSEi extends slide as oil, inflation fears weigh
articles.description: The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) dropped on Thursday, Oct. 1, as investors worried that rising oil prices would push up the inflation rate in September and even October, while the manufacturing index contracted. The main index lost 50.01 points, or 0.88 percent, during Thursday’s trading to close at 5,629.47. The services sector led the decline across the board. Volume was lower but still hefty at 587 million shares worth ₱7.54 billion. Losers outnumbered gainers—113 to 71, with 57 holding steady. “The local index ended lower as selling pressure remained intact amid crude oil prices nearing the $100 per barrel (bbl) level,” said Regina Capital Development Corp. Managing Director Luis Limlingan. Sentiment weakened after the S&P Global Philippines manufacturing purchasing managers’ index (PMI) fell to 49.6 in September from 54.9 in August. Limlingan noted, “The reading marked the first contraction in five months, raising concerns over weakening manufacturing activity and domestic growth.” Philstocks Financial Inc. research manager Japhet Tantiangco said, “The local market extended its decline to a fourth straight day as investors brace for a possibly faster inflation print for September as compared to August. According to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) projections, inflation last month may have settled within 6.4 percent to 7.4 percent, higher than August’s 6.1 percent.” He added that elevated oil prices and yields, together with a weak local currency, also weighed on the market. Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. (RCBC) chief economist Michael Ricafort said the PSEi was lower after most long-term United States (US) Treasury yields hit 24-year highs, making the US dollar attractive due to higher US dollar-denominated interest rate earnings and also increasing bond yields and borrowing costs in some countries around the world.
